newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti critical of welfare document.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti critical of welfare document.

text.p: Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Wednesday that a government document on plans for reforming the country's welfare state represented a "false start."
"What should be in it is not," Bertinotti added after inspecting the document, presented to employers and unions as a basis for talks on reforms.
Bertinotti said that before inspecting the document, Refoundation had stressed that its support was not guaranteed as there had been no meeting to define a common position.
"Today, after seeing the document, we say that we do not share either from a political or programmatic point of view the platform presented by the government," he said.
He said the document contained only a hope to combat unemployment without a policy for employment and said that Refoundation was not convinced by social security proposals.
Union leaders have also criticised the document, with Sergio Cofferati of the CGIL trades union saying it contained "incomprehensible gaps."
Sergio D'Antoni, secretary general of the Cisl trades union, told state Rai radio that the document was "unfair and wrong" and needed to be "thoroughly changed."
"It's clear that if the government's position remains that of today, we are heading for a definitive break."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi presented the document earlier on the first day of talks on welfare state reforms.

Italy is under pressure to carry out a convincing reform of social spending -- and to shake up its pensions system -- to prove that public finances will be kept under control before the planned 1999 launch of the single European currency.
